title: Find and Switch On Battery-Backed Workbench Lighting During a Blackout
instruction: The room lights are out. A lit flashlight is already held in one gripper, pointing straight down; the emergency-light cabinet is not visible at the start. Sweep the work area from left to right with overlapping beam positions to find the glass access case. Keep the case illuminated while the other gripper flips the clear access lid upward, then reach inside, grasp the top bar of the folding U-shaped emergency-light handle, and pull it down to ON. Release it and leave the backup light on.
context: A power cut leaves a workbench dark. A separate battery bank supplies an emergency worklight, but its protected ON handle is outside the robot's initial flashlight beam. The robot must search with the flashlight, keep the control illuminated while opening its cover, then pull the handle to switch on battery-backed lighting. This operates a low-voltage backup lamp; it does not restore mains power.
setup: A fixed 1.1 x 1.3 m YAM station workbench. Ordinary lamps and ambient dome lighting start off. A lit approximately 180 mm, 204 g rigid flashlight begins contact-held by the left gripper near (0.468, 0.214, 0.912 m), pointed at empty bench space. A fixed 180 x 330 mm low access case is centred at (0.35, -0.190 m), with its front toward the overhead/front view, 174 mm side walls and a clear 147 x 150 x 6 mm polycarbonate-look lid on a rear hinge. The lid bears two yellow BACKUP POWER lettering rows; they are unlit until reached by the flashlight. Its 102 x 20 x 20 mm front grip lifts the lid through 0-140 degrees. Inside, a rigid U-shaped handle has 64 mm hinge spacing, 72 mm arms, an 80 x 22 x 18 mm top crossbar and a separate 0-60 degree revolute joint; pulling the bar down actuates the backup light at 48 degrees. The lamp itself is overhead. The case stays fixed; object_jitter=0. The proposed low-voltage reproduction, dimensions and parts are in REAL_TRIAL.md and build_plan.svg.
scoring: The scan path and arm choice are not scored. A lit flashlight lens 8-65 cm from the handle, aimed within 28 degrees of its centre and with an unobstructed ray to it for 10 consecutive 20 Hz steps earns 0.2. From the lid first measurable opening at 0.5 degrees until the first ON crossing, aim and unobstructed line of sight must be maintained every step. A lid opening of at least 115 degrees under continuous illumination earns 0.5. The first handle pull begins at 1.5 degrees from OFF; if it begins before the lid is open 115 degrees, or illumination is lost before ON, the score is irreversibly 0. The handle physically turns on the backup light at 48 degrees even after an invalid sequence, without awarding credit. A one-way catch engages after 50 degrees and blocks reverse travel below 49 degrees, without moving the handle forward. Full score requires a valid first pull, handle at least 48 degrees, lamp on for 10 steps, both grippers at least 5 cm from the top bar, and handle angle varying by no more than 1 degree over 10 consecutive steps. Otherwise the score remains 0.5 after a valid lid opening. The lighting criterion is a pose and ray proxy, not measured lux.
reset_notes: Reset the contact-held lit flashlight to its recorded start pose, shut the rear-hinged lid, release the catch and return the handle to the OFF stop, and turn off backup and ordinary room lights. The case stays fixed and object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Rigid flashlight, polycarbonate-look rear-hinged lid and U-handle move through contact in PhysX. The over-centre lid hold, friction and one-way handle catch are simplified and uncalibrated; the beam intensity is renderer-tuned rather than lux-calibrated. The proposed low-voltage bench fixture is specified for reproduction but has not been physically built or tested.
scores: Scripted YAM demo: 1.0 in 498 steps; Dream-1 beta: 0.2 after the 1,200-step limit on this same scene and scorer
